title: Remove Gemini from Gmail and Docs
summary: One pair of switches turns off the generative features across Gmail, Docs, Sheets and Drive.
changes: The Gemini side panel, "Help me write", smart replies and inbox summaries all disappear. Your documents and mail are untouched.
steps: Open Gmail on the web and go to Settings → See all settings → General.
Find "Google Workspace smart features".
Click "Manage Workspace smart feature settings".
Switch off both toggles: smart features in Workspace, and smart features in other Google products.
Save. Reload Gmail and Docs; the Gemini buttons are gone.
how: Google gates its generative features in Workspace behind the same consent flag as its older "smart" features. Withdrawing that consent removes the whole layer rather than hiding individual buttons.
caveats: It also disables Smart Compose, smart reply, automatic inbox categories and package tracking. Some people miss these; the switch is easy to reverse.
On a work or school account, an administrator may have locked the setting.
Grammar and spelling checks in Docs are part of the same bundle.

sources.title: Turn smart features and personalisation on or off (official)

title: Get the Gemini button out of Google Docs
summary: If you want to keep smart features, you can still remove the writing assistant from the page.
changes: The "Help me write" pill and the Gemini icon leave the document. Everything else stays.
steps: Open any document.
Click the Gemini icon in the top-right, then the settings or three-dot menu inside the panel.
Choose "Bottom bar preferences" and untick "Write with Gemini".
Collapse the side panel with the arrow at its edge.
caveats: It hides the entry points rather than disabling the service. The full switch is the Workspace smart features one above.
Google moves this menu regularly.

alternatives.label: Turn the whole thing off instead

title: Turn off Copilot in Word, Excel and Outlook
summary: Each desktop app has a proper checkbox. Untick it and the button goes away.
changes: The Copilot ribbon button and the margin prompt disappear from that app on that computer.
steps: Open Word. Go to File → Options.
Choose Copilot in the left-hand list.
Untick "Enable Copilot".
Restart Word. Repeat in Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote — the setting is per application.
how: Microsoft added a per-application switch after complaints about the button appearing unbidden. It is stored per device and per app.
caveats: Only available on personal Microsoft accounts. Work and school accounts are controlled by an administrator.
Per computer: repeat on each machine you use.
The web versions of Office have their own, separate controls.

sources.title: Turn Microsoft 365 Copilot on or off (official)

title: Keep the grammar check, lose the ghostwriter
summary: Grammarly separates its generative writing from its corrections. You can keep one.
changes: Suggestions to rewrite or generate whole passages stop appearing. Spelling and grammar corrections remain.
steps: Sign in at account.grammarly.com.
Open Account Settings → Customize or Personalization.
Switch off the generative AI assistance options.
caveats: Grammarly's core checking has always used machine learning; this switch concerns the generative features only.
On a business plan an administrator may control it.

title: Stop your phone finishing your sentences
summary: Predictive text and generated suggestions are separate from autocorrect, and can go alone.
changes: The suggestion strip above the keyboard goes quiet. Autocorrect keeps fixing typos if you want it to.
steps: iPhone: Settings → General → Keyboard. Switch off Predictive. Leave Auto-Correction on if you like it.
iPhone with Apple Intelligence: also turn off Writing Tools under Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri.
Android with Gboard: Settings → System → Languages & input → On-screen keyboard → Gboard → Text correction. Switch off "Show suggestion strip" and "Next-word suggestions".
Samsung Keyboard: Settings → General management → Samsung Keyboard settings → Predictive text off.
caveats: Autocorrect and prediction are different things. Turning off prediction leaves spelling correction intact.
Some keyboards reset these after major updates.

title: Write somewhere that offers nothing
summary: Editors built around a blank page, where nothing suggests, completes or rewrites.
changes: You open the app and there is text and a cursor. Files are plain text on your own disk.
how: These editors store Markdown files in ordinary folders. Obsidian is free for personal use and has no generative features unless you install a plugin; iA Writer marks any pasted text so you always know what you wrote.
caveats: iA Writer and Ulysses are paid. Obsidian is free for personal use.
No real-time collaboration in the Google Docs sense.

title: Quieten Notion's assistant
summary: Stop the AI prompt appearing every time you press space on a new line.
changes: The "Ask AI" hint disappears from empty blocks. The rest of Notion is unchanged.
steps: Open Settings → Preferences (or Notion settings → My settings).
Find the AI section and switch off the inline AI trigger.
Workspace owners can disable Notion AI for the whole workspace under Settings → AI.
caveats: Member-level settings only hide the prompts; a workspace owner must disable the feature entirely.
Notion changes its settings layout frequently.

title: Turn off code completion suggestions
summary: A genuine, complete off switch — both in your account and in the editor.
changes: Suggestions stop appearing as you type. You can turn it off for one language, one file, or entirely.
steps: Visit github.com/settings/copilot to control the account-level subscription and data use.
In VS Code: click the Copilot status icon in the status bar → Disable Completions, globally or for the current language.
In JetBrains IDEs: the Copilot icon in the status bar has the same menu.
To remove it completely, uninstall the extension.
caveats: Organisation-provided Copilot seats may be controlled by your employer.
Turning off completions still leaves the chat panel; disable both if you want silence.

title: Remove Writing Tools from the text menu
summary: Stop "Rewrite", "Proofread" and "Summarise" appearing whenever you select text.
changes: The text selection menu returns to Cut, Copy, Paste and Look Up.
steps: iPhone or iPad: Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri → turn Apple Intelligence off, or turn off Writing Tools specifically.
Mac: System Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri → same controls.
For a permanent block a child or colleague cannot undo: Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions → Intelligence & Siri.
caveats: Turning Apple Intelligence off entirely also removes notification summaries, Clean Up in Photos and the new Siri behaviour. Many people consider that a bonus.
It frees several gigabytes of storage, since the on-device models are deleted.

title: An email client with nothing in the margin
summary: Mail applications that do not offer to write your messages for you.
changes: A compose window with a cursor in it. Nothing suggests, summarises or replies on your behalf.
how: Thunderbird is free, open-source and run by a non-profit; it connects to your existing Gmail or Outlook account and shows you your mail without the web interface's additions.
caveats: Using a separate client does not stop Google or Microsoft processing the mail on their servers. For that you need the Workspace switch above, or a different provider.
Fastmail and Proton are paid services.
